rules.description: Each WAI-ARIA state or property on an element must be one that the element's role supports.
rules.help: Remove the attribute, or give the element the role that supports it.
rules.noFixReason: The attribute may be right and the role wrong (or the reverse); choosing between changing the role and dropping the attribute is a judgement.

rules.description: The role attribute of an element should be one that ARIA in HTML allows on that element.
rules.help: Remove the role, or use an element that suits the role.
rules.noFixReason: Changing the role changes what the element means to users, and which meaning is intended is the author's call.

rules.description: aria-braillelabel needs an accessible name and aria-brailleroledescription needs an aria-roledescription to refine.
rules.help: Add the ordinary label or role description that the braille text abbreviates.
rules.noFixReason: The missing text is content, which only the author can supply.

rules.description: A button, link or menu item given its role by the role attribute must have an accessible name.
rules.help: Give the control a visible text label, an aria-label or an aria-labelledby.
rules.noFixReason: The name is content: only the author knows what the control is called.

rules.description: A native checkbox must not carry an aria-checked value that disagrees with its checked state.
rules.help: Drop aria-checked and let the checked attribute carry the state.
rules.fix: Remove aria-checked from a native checkbox whose value disagrees with the checked attribute. The native state is the one assistive technology reports.

rules.description: The role that applies to an element must not be one that WAI-ARIA or its digital publishing module has deprecated.
rules.help: Replace the deprecated role with the role the specification recommends in its place.
rules.fix: Replace the role directory with list, the replacement WAI-ARIA 1.2 names.

rules.description: A dialog or alert dialog given its role by the role attribute should have an accessible name.
rules.help: Name the dialog with aria-labelledby pointing at its title, or with aria-label.
rules.noFixReason: The name is content: only the author knows what the control is called.

rules.description: The body element must not have aria-hidden="true", which hides the whole page from assistive technology.
rules.help: Remove aria-hidden from body; hide only the parts of the page that need hiding.
rules.fix: Remove aria-hidden="true" from body. No reading of the page is served by hiding all of it.

rules.description: An element with aria-hidden="true" must not contain anything that can receive focus through the Tab key.
rules.help: Make the hidden content non-focusable (tabindex="-1" or disabled), or stop hiding it.
rules.noFixReason: Hiding it from assistive technology, making it unfocusable and showing it are three different outcomes, and the author must choose.

rules.description: A combo box, list box, search box, slider, spin button or text box given its role by the role attribute must have an accessible name.
rules.help: Label the field with a visible label, aria-label or aria-labelledby.
rules.noFixReason: The name is content: only the author knows what the control is called.

rules.description: A meter given its role by the role attribute must have an accessible name.
rules.help: Say what the meter measures with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
rules.noFixReason: The name is content: only the author knows what the control is called.

rules.description: A progress bar given its role by the role attribute must have an accessible name.
rules.help: Say what is progressing with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
rules.noFixReason: The name is content: only the author knows what the control is called.

rules.description: A WAI-ARIA attribute must not be used on a role that prohibits it, such as aria-label on an element with no role.
rules.help: Remove the attribute, or give the element a role that can be named.
rules.fix: Remove the prohibited attribute. Authors may not set it on this role, and removing it leaves the element with the semantics the rest of its markup gives.

rules.description: An element with an explicit role must set the states and properties that role requires.
rules.help: Add the required attribute with a value that matches the element's state.
rules.noFixReason: The value of a required state (checked, the current value of a slider) is the page's own data, so the library cannot choose it.

rules.description: An element whose role needs owned elements (a list needs items, a table needs rows) must contain them.
rules.help: Add the required child elements, or use a role that needs none.
rules.noFixReason: Adding rows, items or options is content, and wrapping existing children can change the page's structure, so the right edit is the author's.

rules.description: An element whose role needs a parent role (a list item needs a list, a tab needs a tab list) must be inside one.
rules.help: Put the element inside an element with the required role, or use a role that needs no parent.
rules.noFixReason: Wrapping orphans in a container changes layout and styling, and which container role is right depends on the content.

rules.description: A role attribute must contain at least one token that names a WAI-ARIA role authors may use.
rules.help: Correct the role name, or remove the attribute and use an element that already has the meaning.
rules.noFixReason: Passing a list of tokens when one of them is valid is allowed (fallback roles), so a failure means no token is usable and the intended role is unknown.

rules.description: A tab given its role by the role attribute must have an accessible name.
rules.help: Give the tab text, an aria-label or an aria-labelledby.
rules.noFixReason: The name is content: only the author knows what the control is called.

rules.description: An element with role="text" must not contain focusable elements.
rules.help: Move the focusable element out of the role="text" element, or remove the role.
rules.noFixReason: Moving a control or dropping the role changes the page's structure, which is an authoring decision.

rules.description: A checkbox, radio button, switch, option or toggling menu item given its role by the role attribute must have an accessible name.
rules.help: Label the control with text, aria-label or aria-labelledby.
rules.noFixReason: The name is content: only the author knows what the control is called.

rules.description: A tooltip given its role by the role attribute must have an accessible name.
rules.help: Give the tooltip text content, an aria-label or an aria-labelledby.
rules.noFixReason: The name is content: only the author knows what the control is called.

rules.description: A tree item given its role by the role attribute should have an accessible name.
rules.help: Give the tree item text, an aria-label or an aria-labelledby.
rules.noFixReason: The name is content: only the author knows what the control is called.

rules.description: Every attribute that starts with aria- must be a state or property defined by WAI-ARIA.
rules.help: Fix the spelling of the attribute, or remove it if WAI-ARIA has no such state or property.
rules.fix: Remove the aria- attribute that WAI-ARIA does not define. A browser ignores it, so removing it changes nothing a user perceives.

rules.description: Every non-empty WAI-ARIA state or property must have a value of its type, and a required ID reference must name an element in the page.
rules.help: Use one of the values WAI-ARIA allows for the attribute, or point the required reference at an element that exists.
rules.fix: Remove an attribute whose value is outside its type when the role does not require that attribute. A browser already falls back to the attribute's default, so removing it changes nothing a user perceives.

rules.description: An element marked as decorative must really be presentational: it may not be focusable or carry a global WAI-ARIA attribute.
rules.help: Either make the element non-interactive without WAI-ARIA attributes, or drop the presentational role and give it a real one.
rules.noFixReason: Two fixes exist (remove the role or remove what conflicts with it) and which one is right depends on the author's intent.

rules.description: An element whose role makes its children presentational (a button, a tab, an image) must not contain anything reachable with the Tab key.
rules.help: Move the focusable element out, or change the outer role to one that exposes its children.
rules.noFixReason: Removing the focusable child, moving it or changing the outer role each change the page; the author must choose.
